BR.name: Cardo-amarelo
BR.citation: PFAF Plant Database; also documented as cardo-santa, figo-do-inferno, papoula-de-espinho

IN.name: Satyanashi
IN.citation: Wikipedia; peer-reviewed pharmacognosy review (Revista Brasileira de Farmacognosia, 2013). Name means 'destroyer of truth/destroyer of all', referencing the plant's severe toxicity - its seed oil (argemone/katkar oil) contains sanguinarine and has caused documented mass poisoning outbreaks ('epidemic dropsy') when it adulterates mustard oil. Also flowers prominently during the Holi/Holika Dahan festival season

MX.name: Chicalote
MX.citation: PFAF Plant Database; Nahuatl-derived name. Native to Mexico, used medicinally by Indigenous peoples there and in the western United States for centuries. Also documented as adormidera espinosa, cardo blanco

US.name: Mexican prickly poppy
US.citation: GBIF; Wikipedia. Used medicinally by Indigenous peoples of the western United States. SAFETY: contains the toxic alkaloids sanguinarine and dihydrosanguinarine; toxic to grazing animals
